narrative: Material PL1__M941007A exhibits high-volume, smooth daily demand (CV=0.27) well described by a normal distribution with no statistically significant trend. Lead times are variable (CV=0.46) with a bimodal distribution between ~1.6 and ~3.6-4.2 day cycles, which dominates the uncertainty buffer at 88.6% of total variance. The current SAP policy holds zero safety stock and triggers near-daily replenishments at MOQ=542, generating excessive ordering costs. The recommended (r,Q) policy with SS=4,344 and OQ=7,138 achieves the 95% service level while cutting total annual cost by over 80%.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint binding: EOQ reduced from 9199 to 7138 units (SS=4344 + OQ=7138 = 11482 <= 11482.97)
SAP safety stock is 0 — material currently has no buffer against lead time variability
Lead time CV=0.459 classified as VARIABLE; lead time variability is dominant risk factor

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth, high-volume, near-normal daily demand with variable but non-intermittent lead times is the textbook fit for a classical (r,Q) framework. EOQ minimises total ordering and holding cost; the reorder point absorbs lead-time variability at the target 95% service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap of 11,482.97 units reduces order quantity from unconstrained EOQ of 9,199 to 7,138 units, modestly increasing annual order frequency (75 vs 58 orders/year). Service level is maintained; cost penalty is minor (~8% above unconstrained optimum).
